title: OpenAI Responses v2-preview: deterministic-hint forwarding and attribute passthrough for streaming
author: Sofia Patel
description:
This PR adds compatibility shims and server-side plumbing to support the OpenAI 'responses v2-preview' surface for newer client variants while preserving deterministic behavior hints and per-response attribute passthrough during streaming. Motivation: customers expect parity with the latest OpenAI Responses semantics (determinism_hint/deterministic_hint, attribute metadata propagation, and more granular streaming control) while keeping Redwood's stable reassembly and tool/function-call handoff behavior. Changes here intentionally avoid changing runtime RNG semantics; instead we forward user-supplied hints and metadata to downstream model adapters and persist attributes in response envelopes for observability and routing.

What this PR does (high level): 
- Introduces a lightweight 'deterministic-hint' header/field mapping layer that accepts several upstream keys (seed, deterministic, determinism_hint) and normalizes them to a canonical intermediate field that model adapters can consume. 
- Implements attribute passthrough for Responses v2-preview: incoming request-level metadata in 'attributes' and 'response_attributes' is routed into the streaming envelope and preserved on final assembled Responses. This includes user-provided tags, toolcall context ids, and opaque routing hints. 
- Stabilizes streaming reassembly by adding boundary markers and resume tokens to the chunk stream; the reassembler uses these markers to avoid duplicate toolcall dispatch after reconnects. 
- Ensures tool/function-calls invoked mid-stream still receive the normalized determinism hint and attributes. Tool call handoff now attaches an 'x-rw-deterministic-hint' header and 'x-rw-attr-string' as part of the call metadata. 
- Adds end-to-end tests and integration harness updates for both OpenAI-compatibility mode and Redwood-native mode, covering chunk loss/reorder scenarios, resume semantics, and seeded replay. 

Files touched (examples): src/server/openai_compat/resp_v2_adapter.py, src/server/streaming/reassembler.py, src/server/tooling/tool_call_proxy.py, tests/integration/resp_v2_resume_tests.py, docs/openai_compat/RESP-V2-mapping.md, api/compat_mappings.yaml 

Compatibility notes and non-goals: 
- This PR forwards determinism hints only; it does not alter the RNG implementation or guarantee byte-for-byte deterministic outputs across model versions. Customers can use the hints for best-effort determinism or to tag requests for deterministic experiments. 
- We intentionally keep the envelope fields extensible; new attributes are tolerated and persisted as opaque key/value pairs. 
- Rolling out is gated behind a feature flag 'openai_resp_v2_preview' to allow staged enablement and telemetry collection.

Testing and rollout plan: 
- Unit tests for canonicalization and header mapping. 
- Integration tests simulating chunk loss and client reconnects to validate resume tokens and event deduplication. 
- A/B rollout: enable flag for 5% of traffic for one day, then 25% for three days, followed by full rollout if error budget remains healthy. 

Checklist: 
- [x] Map upstream determinism keys to canonical field
- [x] Preserve attributes in streaming envelope and final response
- [x] Attach determinism/attributes to tool/function call metadata
- [x] Add integration tests for resume & dedupe
- [x] Docs for mapping and migration notes

Related: ENG-9812 (Responses v2 compatibility), PM-430 (product impact assessment), SUP-1122 (customer request for metadata passthrough).
